newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Thistle Hotels sets slim premium on debut.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Thistle Hotels sets slim premium on debut.

text.p: Thistle Hotels on Wednesday made its stock market debut in a flotation valuing London's biggest hotel group at 1.05 billion pounds ($1.6 billion).
Chairman Robert Peel said he was pleased with the results of the flotation and denied suggestions the company had joined the market near a peak in hotel demand.
He said he had personally bought about 575,000 of the shares on offer and was gratified that they had gone to a slim premium in early trading.

After rising as high as 175 pence ($2.73), the stock later slipped back to close at 172-1/2 pence ($2.69) compared with the 170 pence ($2.65) flotation price confirmed earlier by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd whose stake in Thistle falls to 46 percent from 70 percent as a result of the float.
Thistle, formerly Mount Charlotte Group until it was taken over by Brierley in 1990, saw volume of some 34.27 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock in London.
